title: Have You Told Them?
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This reflection urges readers to actually voice pride in the people who shaped them, rather than let it go unsaid. It explores why this feels so uncomfortable: expressing pride can feel vulnerable, gushing, or like an admission of one's own insecurities. The piece offers alternative phrasings beyond "I'm proud of you" that make the sentiment easier to share more often. It closes with a direct call to action, framing silence as a theft of joy from both the giver and receiver of unspoken admiration.
points: Names specific emotional barriers that keep people from voicing pride in others

Closes with a direct call to tell influential people you're proud of them
quotes: Telling others who have made a major impact on us that we are proud of them is the rocket fuel of positive emotion.
Saying out loud that we are proud of them sounds like a gushing gob of sweetness reserved only for the wide-eyed amazement of obsequious people.
Here's an inside secret. If you are truly proud of someone, you need to tell them.
You will experience the warm sensation that only the most honest human connection can produce.
Not telling them frequently robs them of a joy no one else can give them.
Keeping your pride in them to yourself steals from you the satisfaction of deep emotional connection to those you care most about.
